chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hanifah, from Abi Hanifah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'How is it that two witnesses are sufficient for Qatl (killing), whereas for Zina (adultery/fornication) four witnesses are required, and killing is more severe than adultery?' He said: 'Because Qatl is a single action, whereas Zina is two actions; therefore, it is not permissible in it except with four witnesses: two witnesses for the man and two witnesses for the woman.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Islamic law require four witnesses for adultery but only two for killing?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a jurisprudential rationale for the disparity in witness counts between Qatl (homicide) and Zina (adultery). He distinguishes that Zina involves two distinct actions by two parties, necessitating four witnesses (two per person), whereas Qatl is viewed as a singular act requiring only two witnesses. This reasoning highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the structural nature of the offense in determining evidentiary requirements.
